solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gear up for game of cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means read the word from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone kits themselves out ready for an evening of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag is an old British card game, a forerunner of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Brag is a three-card gambling game, so it is a game of cards.

clue.text: Various wetland birds, maybe

definitions.meaning: an old adjective for several or sundry, found in legal and biblical English
water birds that plunge under the surface, also called loons

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note of assorted waterbirds seen in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The old adjective 'divers' (as in 'divers reasons') means various; 'maybe' flags that divers are just one example of wetland birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic adjective for several or sundry, and divers are diving water birds.

clue.text: Challenging attitude of French husband-to-be

indicators.note: tells you to put 'of' into French

parts.note: a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A remark about the stroppy manner of a Frenchman's intended groom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of French' reads like a description of the husband-to-be, but it is an instruction to translate the word 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is an attitude of open challenge or resistance.

clue.text: Absolutely explosive noise

definitions.meaning: informal British adverb for exactly or completely, used before 'on time' or 'up to date'

explanation.surface: An emphatic description of a truly deafening blast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British informal English 'bang' is an adverb meaning exactly or completely: bang up to date, bang in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang can mean absolutely or exactly, and it is also the loud noise of an explosion.

clue.text: Crayon left stuck under glue

parts.note: paste is a kind of glue

explanation.surface: A child's crayon has been abandoned, gummed up in a pot of glue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a craft table; in a down clue 'under' means the L goes after PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a crayon made of pressed coloured powder.

clue.text: Type of convection heater in new farriery

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some new heating gadget installed at a blacksmith's forge.
explanation.walkthrough: Farriery is the craft of shoeing horses, which suits heaters and forges but has nothing to do with the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An air fryer cooks by blowing hot air around food, which is convection heating.

clue.text: Work teams gathered for ship's voyage

indicators.note: 'I gather' means 'I hear', so gathered signals a sound-alike

parts.note: work teams on a ship are crews, and that word is said just like the voyage

explanation.surface: Staff teams are assembled to go on a sea trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' seems to mean assembled, which fits crews on a ship; here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a holiday trip on a liner, calling at ports, is the ship's voyage in question.

clue.text: Slow movement beginning to affect soldier in trouble

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'affect'

explanation.surface: A soldier in difficulty moves sluggishly at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a soldier on the march; it is a section of a piece of music. GI is the standard label for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term: the tempo marking for 'at ease' names a slow section of a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Nodding perhaps is a salutation without talking primarily

indicators.note: remove a letter from the greeting
take the first letter of 'talking'

parts.note: first letter of talking, removed from GREETING

explanation.surface: A silent nod of the head counts as saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the nod a hello; take the T out of A GREETING. 'Perhaps' marks nodding as just one way of agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a common way of showing that you are agreeing.

clue.text: Vegan stir-fry option needing some hint of umami

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

explanation.surface: Meat-free stir-fry advice: tofu wants a savoury umami touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint of' looks like it wants a first letter; the answer instead runs across the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, bean curd, is a common plant-based protein for stir-fries.

clue.text: A boy or girl?

parts.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a baby is male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a person, while 'A boy' also builds the word: PER for 'a' and SON for 'boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example read straight: any child, boy or girl, is an individual human, while 'A boy' also spells it out.

clue.text: Inspector, formerly a pit worker

parts.note: a miner works in a pit

explanation.surface: A mining inspector's career history: he once worked down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: A pit is a coal mine, so a pit worker is a miner.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner inspects things closely, so is an inspector.

clue.text: Comeback absolutely devoid of energy

indicators.note: being devoid of something means lacking it, so the word must lose that letter

explanation.surface: A sports team's recovery came with nothing left in the tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an exhausted team fighting back; E is the physics symbol for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a recovery, a comeback after falling behind.

clue.text: Pursue support involving peacekeeping organisation

parts.note: a rafter is a roof support beam

explanation.surface: Chase backing for a mission from the UN peacekeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' suggests backing for a cause; here it is a beam holding up a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: chasing someone on foot, or courting them eagerly, is pursuing them.

clue.text: Copper suppresses resistance in wine-producing region

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman crushes an uprising in wine country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a policeman; here it is the element Cu. A cru is a French vineyard or wine-growing area.
explanation.definitionFit: Cru, French for growth, names a vineyard or wine-producing area, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Lower area alongside HQ

parts.note: headquarters, the home station of an army or firm

explanation.surface: Directions to a lower zone next to headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as an adjective describing the area; it is the verb, as in to lower oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to bring someone down in dignity or rank, often oneself, is to lower them.

clue.text: Family member finally kinda let loose?

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'kinda'

parts.note: to untie is to let loose

explanation.surface: A relative who at last sort of let her hair down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a relative who finally relaxed a bit; 'kinda' is slang for kind of.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a parent's sister, in the affectionate form, is one family member.

clue.text: Kind of fancy tea urn

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, made over into a new form

explanation.surface: Something like a posh tea urn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of fancy' reads as sort of posh; 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature means kind or sort, as in 'problems of this nature'.

clue.text: It's set out to collect the church donations

indicators.note: the letters of IT'S are set out afresh

explanation.surface: The collection plate has been put out for the congregation's offerings.
explanation.walkthrough: TI(THE)S. 'Set out to collect' reads as a single phrase about the collection plate; it holds two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithes are a tenth of income given to the church.

clue.text: Traveller to Oz initially lived in the middle of Wollongong

indicators.note: take the first letters of 'lived in'

parts.note: first letters of lived and in

indicators.note: take the two central letters of Wollongong

parts.note: WollONgong, the fifth and sixth of ten letters

explanation.surface: A visitor to Australia first settled in central Wollongong.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is slang for Australia, and Wollongong is an Australian city, but the Oz here is the Wizard's land: the Cowardly Lion travels there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cowardly Lion journeys to the Emerald City in The Wizard of Oz.

clue.text: Staff go around back of theatre, unseen by an audience

indicators.note: the letters are moved around
take the last letter of theatre

parts.note: last letter of theatre, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: Stagehands walk behind the set, out of the public's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally about staff going off stage, which is why the anagram is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything off-stage happens out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Managed to get rid of top column with a slant?

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone managed to remove the top of a leaning pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' pretends to be a pillar; it is a newspaper column. An op-ed is an opinion piece, opposite the editorial page.
explanation.definitionFit: An op-ed is an opinion column in a newspaper, written from a particular slant.

clue.text: Unpleasant characters appearing regularly in gory instant message

indicators.note: take every other letter of gory

explanation.surface: A horrible person turns up often in a gruesome text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people; it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bleak news or a dismal outlook can be called unpleasant.

clue.text: Live re-interpretation of Desire

indicators.note: the letters are read in a new way

explanation.surface: A live new version of a song or play called Desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as the adjective, a live performance; it is the verb, to live somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: making your home at an address is to live there.

clue.text: Piece from the Met I consider vomit-inducing

indicators.note: the answer is a piece taken from the following words

explanation.surface: An art critic finds a work in the Metropolitan Museum sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, so 'Piece' looks like an artwork; it means a piece of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term used as an adjective: a substance given to make a patient sick is vomit-inducing.
